evals.name: check-verifies-the-linter-actually-executes
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, markdownlint-cli2 resolution AND liveness, the consumer markdownlint config cascade, gitignored-path scope, the markdown_format_enabled toggle, and hook registration — one remediation line per FAIL, nothing modified.
expectations: Resolves markdownlint-cli2 exactly the way the hook does, including its symlink/escape validation of a repo-local shim, so a shim the hook would reject does not PASS here
Goes past resolution to liveness: runs the resolved tool with --version, and treats resolution without successful execution as FAIL with the execution error in the remediation line
Names the concrete broken-shim causes the liveness probe catches — a missing Node interpreter or a dangling target
Reports the effective markdown_format_lint_gitignored value and treats unexpanded or empty as the default false, meaning gitignored Markdown is skipped

evals.name: no-markdownlint-config-inverts-the-jq-verdict
evals.prompt:
/markdown-format:setup check

There is no markdownlint config in this repo and jq isn't installed either. What is actually wrong?
evals.expected_output: Answers that the missing config, not jq, is why nothing happens: the hook decides the opt-in first and emits nothing at all without it, so jq's absence is INFO here rather than the usual FAIL, and the un-opted-in path is reported as INFO — inactive, not PASS.
expectations: Downgrades the missing jq to INFO in this state and says explicitly that the missing config, not jq, is why nothing happens
Reports the hook as INFO — inactive, not PASS — for a path no config governs, and states that without the opt-in there is no --fix, no findings, and no notice of any kind
Never reports markdownlint's own default rules as the fallback — an unconfigured repo gets no rules, not the defaults
Leads with the missing config rather than burying it under passing prerequisites, and names the remediation in the same line

evals.name: config-cascade-is-per-path-not-repo-wide
evals.prompt:
/markdown-format:setup check

We have a markdownlint config under docs/ but none at the repo root. Is the whole repo covered?
evals.expected_output: No: the opt-in is per-path, mirroring the hook's walk from an edited file's directory up to the repo root, so a nested config covers only its own subtree while a root config would cover the tree. Reports the root config the cascade discovers (or its absence) and lists nested configs with their directory scope.
expectations: States that the opt-in is per-path and that a nested config covers only its own subtree while a root config covers the tree
Searches the whole tree while skipping node_modules, and lists each nested config with the directory scope it governs
Surfaces the README's configuration trust boundary for every config the hook's own risk collection would flag
Does not report the repo as covered on the strength of a nested config alone

evals.name: bare-apply-neither-installs-nor-writes-rules
evals.prompt:
/markdown-format:setup apply

markdownlint-cli2 isn't installed and we have no config. Set it up — install the linter and pick sensible rules for us.
evals.expected_output: Bare apply installs nothing: the dependency install runs only under the explicit `apply install-lint` invocation, through the repository's own package manager resolved from its lockfile or packageManager field. Declines to pick rules — a minimal config is offered only when explicitly asked, because which rules a repository adopts is its own decision.
expectations: Does not install markdownlint-cli2 from bare apply — states that install-lint is the explicit argument that authorizes it
Does not choose or write a rule set; offers a minimal config only as an explicitly-requested action
Never introduces a competing lockfile: with no package.json, an ambiguous multi-lockfile state, or a lockfile contradicting packageManager, it stops with manager-specific guidance instead of guessing
Never installs system packages and never writes Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/markdown-format:setup apply

Everything was green ten minutes ago. Run it again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change on the second pass.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not re-run a dependency install that already succeeded
Lints, fixes, and touches no repository content — the only execution check performs is the harmless --version liveness probe

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/markdown-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install markdown-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config markdown_format_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (verified on Claude Code 2.1.240), rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config markdown_format_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for, and notes the flag is repeatable for the second key markdown_format_lint_gitignored

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option including the gitignored-lint key to its manifest default
Carries the CLI version the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim was verified on — the literal 2.1.240 — and scopes it to a non-sensitive option at user scope
Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect
